parameters.content:
## 1. Discover and extract tenders (two lanes, one standard tender object)
**API lane** (top): public JSON APIs described in Config (`request`, `records`, `fields`). No LLM, no Firecrawl.
**URL lane** (bottom): ANY site: the tender list, one notice or just the home page. The **Tender Scout Agent** opens pages with its tool `open_page` (Scout Tools sub-workflow: Firecrawl + numbered links): from a home page it finds the tender list, follows the next pages, and answers with the **ids** of the tender links (it never writes a tender URL; URL3 maps the ids back). Then Firecrawl reads each tender, the extract LLM fills the fields, code verifies them against the page.

## 2. Clean, then ONE analysis call per kept tender
Clean = facts in code (dates, awards, expiry, duplicates). Analysis = type + fit + proof quote + requirements (only when fit is high/medium). Code verifies the quote and every requirement.

## 3. Research only the buyers of fit tenders
The agent calls the tools; **Parse Research** builds the profile from the tool results with name / domain gates. The agent never writes facts into the profile directly.

## Models
Pick the provider in `00 - Config` (`LLM_PROVIDER`), the model name in its node.
n8n loads **every** connected model on each call: give each Model node a credential (a placeholder key is fine for providers you do not use) and do not disable them.

## 4. Match requirements with your knowledge base (RAG)
The RAG service of your team returns the requirements matrix (covered / partial / missing + proof document) and fit scores. **Join RAG** keeps its status per requirement.

## 5. Competitor & Budget Agent (market study)
For the best fit tenders: the agent searches awarded contracts (TED for France / EU, DECP for France) by CPV and keywords, plus the buyer's own past awards, and **chooses the comparable ones by id**. **Parse Market** computes the budget range (25th-75th percentile), the competitors (who won them) and the usual number of bids from those rows; sentences with numbers not in the data are removed.

## 6. Rank, export, hand off to the proposal studio
**Build Proposal Input** = one JSON per fit tender (contract in INTEGRATION.md) + a file with all of them (the full v2). **Adapt for Studio** = the copy the studio gets: no demo record or weak proof shown as proof, the proposed team and its certifications, no budget the market study does not support, the studio's default template. **Send to Proposal Service** POSTs it to the studio's tender inbox (Config proposal.url, credential "Proposal Studio key"). **Start Deck** starts the deck of the rank-1 tender (Config proposal.autoDeck 'top1'; 'none' = every deck from the interface). Run Summary = the run report.

options.systemMessage:
You find the CURRENT calls for tenders (public procurement notices) published on ONE website, with the tool open_page.
Code checks everything you report against what the tool returned, so only use ids and URLs that the tool showed you.
open_page returns the page id, the start of its text, then its same-site links, one per line: [id] link text — context | url
HOW TO WORK
1. Call open_page with the START URL (then with each OTHER PAGE given in the task).
2. If the START page is itself ONE tender notice (one buyer, one object, its own dates): its PAGE id is the only tender.
   Open no other page and answer.
3. If the page lists tenders: note the ids of the links that each open ONE tender / call for bids / consultation notice.
   open_page shows the list's next page as "NEXT PAGE: [id] | url": while you have pages left, open it and note its tenders too.
4. If the page is not the list of current tenders (home page, menu, section page, a page with only a few "latest" notices):
   open the ONE link that most likely leads to that list (e.g. "Appels d'offres", "Marchés publics", "Consultations",
   "Tenders", "Procurement", "طلبات العروض", "الصفقات العمومية"), then continue from step 3.
RULES
- ONE page per open_page call, one call at a time (never several calls at once): every page costs a credit.
- Open only URLs written in a tool result or in the task, each URL at most once, and never more pages than allowed.
- Do not open the tender notices themselves: their ids on the list are enough.
- Not tenders: news, events, jobs, categories, filters, sorting, search, pagination, login, contact, social and help pages.
FINAL ANSWER: ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"tender_links":["id","id"],"list_url":"URL of the page that lists the tenders, or null"}

parameters.description: Any website. Open ONE page and get its id, the start of its text, its NEXT PAGE (if it is a list) and its same-site links, each as: [id] link text — context | url. Input url: a full https URL from the task or from an earlier open_page result.

options.systemMessage:
You research ONE organisation that published a public tender, by calling tools. Code checks every fact against the tool results, so only report what the tools returned.
GOAL: official website, contact email and phone, past tenders or contracts, supervising bodies or partners, size or budget signals.
RULES
- Several tools cover ONE country only (see each tool description). Call them only when COUNTRY matches.
- First call: wikidata_lookup with the buyer name (when the task gives BUYER SIREN: registry_search with that SIREN first).
- BUYER SIREN (France) is the buyer's own number, given by the tender notice: call registry_search with q = that 9-digit SIREN before any registry search by name, then decp_awards with it. The row with that siren IS the buyer, whatever its legal name; a registry row or a Wikidata siren= with another siren is another organisation, even when it shares the buyer's acronym.
- When the registry tool applies and finds no match, retry it ONCE with a shorter name (without the administrative prefix, e.g. "Ville de", "Commune de", "Ministry of").
- If the buyer name is an acronym or a short name and wikidata_lookup shows a longer official name for it, call registry_search with that official name (and boamp_history too when the first one found nothing).
- When the task gives ALSO SEARCH AS, use that name too when a search under the full name finds no matching row.
- When registry_search gives the buyer's siren (France), call decp_awards with it in your NEXT step (it needs that siren): its contracts give amounts and numbers of bids.
- boamp_history: call it with the buyer name exactly as written after BUYER (the name its notices publish), never with the registry's legal name.
- web_search: ALWAYS call it at least once when no website was given in the tender: the buyer name plus the country name, written in the buyer's LANGUAGE (LANGUAGE fr: French words such as "site officiel", never English). If no official site appears, retry ONCE with another query (the name with its town or its activity).
- buyer_type: when registry_search matched the buyer, public=yes means one of local_authority, regional_authority, state_administration, public_agency, health, education_research, and public=mixed means public_company; never private_company.
- registry staff= is a BAND of employees (staff=100-199: between 100 and 199), never an exact number.
- web_scrape: only pages of the buyer's own website (contact or about page), at most 2 pages.
- Never repeat an identical call. At most 8 calls.
- Before the final answer: decp_awards must have been called (France, when registry_search gave the siren) and web_search too (when no website was given). If not, call them first.
FINAL ANSWER: ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"buyer_type":"local_authority|regional_authority|state_administration|public_agency|public_company|health|education_research|private_company|other|unknown","size_hint":"small|medium|large|unknown","summary":"1 to 3 sentences, only facts read in the tool results","official_website":"https://... or null"}

parameters.description: Any country. Look up an organisation on Wikidata. Returns up to 2 lines: label, description, country, SIREN (France), official website, employees and revenue (with year) when known. Namesakes abroad are other bodies. Input q: the organisation name.

FRANCE ONLY. Search the French company and administration registry by name or by 9-digit SIREN. Returns up to 5 lines: legal name, siren, siret, address, legal form, public body (yes / mixed = SEM, a mixed-economy company with majority public capital / no), staff band (a range of employees, e.g. 100-199), revenue when known. Input q: the 9-digit BUYER SIREN when the task gives one, else the buyer name.

options.systemMessage:
You study the MARKET of ONE public tender for a company that will bid on it: which AWARDED contracts are comparable, at what
price, and who won them. Code computes the budget range and the competitors from the contracts YOU choose, so choose carefully.
Each tool row is one awarded contract: AWARD | id | date | amount= | cur= | buyer= | winners= | bids= | cpv= | fw= | src= | title=
(fw=yes: a framework agreement, its amount is often a ceiling, not a price).
HOW TO WORK
1. Call similar_awards with the tender's CPV codes cut to their 2 or 3 first digits (72 = IT services, 48 = software packages;
   a full 8-digit code finds few contracts) and 1 to 3 short keywords of the title, in the tender's language (for Tunisia: in
   French, even when the tender is in Arabic): the words that name the deliverable or its acronym ("LLM", "billetterie"),
   never generic ones alone ("agents", "services", "solution").
2. If a call returns no row, or fewer than 5 rows are comparable, call it again with broader keywords or a broader CPV; if most
   rows are unrelated, narrower.
3. Call buyer_awards with the buyer name (and the siren when the task gives one).
4. Choose the COMPARABLE contracts: the same kind of deliverable and a similar scope (not hardware supply for a software tender,
   not a national framework for a small local project). Several buyers are fine. Never leave out a row with an amount and fw=no
   whose title names the tender's deliverable: it is the best price reference.
RULES: at most 3 tool calls (their results are long and your memory is small); never repeat an identical call; use only ids
returned by the tools. If no tool returns rows (for example a country without public award data), answer with an empty list and say so.
FINAL ANSWER: ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"comparable_ids":["id","id"],"positioning":"2 to 4 sentences: who usually wins this kind of contract, how many bids to expect, how to position the bid. Only facts from the rows.","budget_comment":"one sentence on the likely budget, only from the rows"}

parameters.description: France, other EU countries and Tunisia. Awarded contracts of ANY buyer similar to a tender, newest first (TED; DECP for France; TUNEPS for Tunisia, amounts in TND). Inputs: cpv = CPV prefixes of 2 or 3 digits separated by commas (e.g. "72, 48"; a full 8-digit code finds few contracts); query = 1 to 3 short keywords or phrases of the tender title separated by commas (each one is searched; in France by its acronym or its most specific word, so "agents LLM" searches LLM), in its language (REQUIRED for Tunisia: TUNEPS has no CPV; its titles are in French, so French keywords find the most, and it matches them literally, as titles write them: "gestion des licences", not "gestion licences"); country = 2-letter country code of the buyer (FR, BE, TN ...).

value.query: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('query', `Short keywords of the tender title, comma separated`, 'string', '') }}

parameters.description: France, other EU countries and Tunisia. Contracts THIS buyer awarded in the last 3 years (amount, winners, bids). Inputs: buyer_name = the buyer name as published; siren = its 9-digit SIREN if known (France; without it, France is searched by buyer name), else empty; cpv = optional CPV prefix to keep only similar contracts (e.g. 72); country = 2-letter country code.

value.siren: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('siren', `9-digit SIREN of the buyer, or empty`, 'string', '') }}

nodes.name: Adapt for Studio
nodes.notes: The copy the proposal studio receives: demo records, weak proofs, header lines, non-team CVs and an unsupported budget left out (counted in studio_adapter). Build Proposal Input's file stays the full v2.

nodes.name: Send to Proposal Service
nodes.notes: Stores each proposal input in the proposal studio's tender inbox (contract olivesoft.proposal-input.v2, see INTEGRATION.md): Config proposal.url, credential "Proposal Studio key" (header X-API-Key). Answer {status: "ok", id}: one tender per tender_id, a new run replaces it.

nodes.name: Start Deck
nodes.notes: Starts the deck of the rank-1 tender in the proposal studio (Config proposal.autoDeck 'top1'): 202 {runId}. 409 (another deck is being generated), 503 (generation not configured), 502 (deck agents unreachable) are only reported by Run Summary.

nodes.name: Save to Google Sheet
nodes.notes: OPTIONAL persistence keyed on tender_id; canonical_id and pair_key columns feed the known-ids check of the next run.
